questions.question: State the strict and expanded definitions of unemployment, give the rate's correct denominator, and describe the six features of South African unemployment with an implication for each.
questions.expected_answer: Strict: working age, without work, available to start, and actively seeking. Expanded: adds discouraged work-seekers who want work but have stopped searching. The rate divides the unemployed by the labour force — employed plus unemployed — never by the whole population. Features: chiefly structural — it survives upswings, so the cycle alone cannot explain it; youth-heavy — under-35 rates far above the national figure, first-time seekers waiting longest; skill-sorted — joblessness collapses as qualifications rise while skilled posts go unfilled; geographic — deepest in former homelands and outer townships, an inherited spatial cost; long-duration — many have searched over a year, and each idle month erodes skills, networks and confidence; and a wide discouragement band — the expanded rate sits several points above the strict one, so always ask which measure a headline quotes. Implications: growth without labour absorption will not clear it, and remedies must reach the young and long-term unemployed whom the market bypasses.

questions.question: Diagnose the five types of unemployment from scenarios and match each to its remedy, then sort the consequences across three levels and state the self-feeding loop.
questions.expected_answer: Frictional — the gap between jobs, like a graduate awaiting a start date; remedy: information and faster matching. Structural — mismatch of skills or location against employer needs, like the machinist whose craft no growing sector wants; South Africa's dominant type; remedy: education, technical training, retraining and shrinking the distance between people and work. Cyclical — downswing retrenchments; remedy: restored demand through spending, credit and exports. Seasonal — calendar-shaped work like fruit-packing; remedy: diversification and off-season income or training. Technological — tasks absorbed by machines; remedy: retraining toward work machines cannot do. Consequences — individual: lost income, poverty, dependence, eroding skills and confidence, tolls on health and dignity; economy: output forgone inside the PPC, weaker aggregate demand, a fiscus collecting less while spending more, decaying future capacity; society: deeper poverty and inequality, an excluded young generation, strain on stability. The loop: no wage means no spending, no spending no orders, no orders no hiring — solutions attempt to cut it.

questions.question: Evaluate the three approaches to solving unemployment — growth of production, public employment programmes and unemployment insurance — with strengths and limits, ending with the diagnose-before-prescribing conclusion.
questions.expected_answer: Growth of production: derived demand creates durable, self-financing jobs; policies include investment, infrastructure, support for labour-absorbing sectors like agriculture, tourism and construction, small-enterprise development and export promotion; limit — composition decides everything, since capital-intensive growth lifts output while hiring few. Public employment programmes, with the Expanded Public Works Programme as the standing example: immediate income, a first work record and public assets; limits — temporary, modestly paid, budget-funded with an opportunity cost, and needing onward connections to skills or employers — a bridge judged by where it lands. Unemployment insurance: one percent from worker matched by employer funds temporary benefits plus maternity, illness and dependant cover; strengths — softens the income shock, buys search time, steadies spending in downswings; limits — partial, time-bound, and reaching only former contributors, so the never-employed young stand outside the net. Conclusion: cyclical needs demand, frictional needs information, structural needs skills, mobility and labour-absorbing growth, with bridges and nets supporting — no single instrument suffices, and diagnosis precedes prescription.
